b201.text: Last time, Basil touched a mimosa, and its leaves folded up. It was not shy. It was responding to a change. Now we are on a farm in Kranji.

b301.text: Lock in first. And find the new lizard!

b401.text: Five eggs. So five chicks. Every egg hatches!

b402.text: Round one. Is Momo right? Does every egg hatch? One, yes. Two, no. Show me with your fingers.

b404.text: One. The hen kept all five warm.

b405.text: Two! Lizards lay eggs too. Grandma says not every egg hatches.

b407.text: A crack. A beak. One chick! Two. Three. Four!

b408.text: One egg did not hatch. The answer is two. Not every egg hatches.

b410.text: That happens, Momo. It is why some animals lay many eggs.

b501.text: Yesterday, one hen. Today, one hen and four chicks.

b503.text: When living things reproduce, there will be more of them. The ability to reproduce is important to ensure the survival of all living things.

b504.text: Some animals reproduce by giving birth to their young alive.

b505.text: Kittens! I was born like that too.

b506.text: Other animals lay eggs and their young hatch out of the eggs.

b508.text: Some plants reproduce by producing seeds.

b510.text: Other plants can reproduce through spores.

b511.text: Like this fern. Look under the leaf.

b601.text: Why does reproducing matter? Without new young, a kind of living thing would disappear forever. Scientists call that extinct.

b701.text: And the four chicks? Now they will grow.

b702.text: So a chick just gets bigger? A giant chick?

b703.text: Not a giant chick. Look at the hen. Bigger, yes. But she also has wing feathers, a red comb and a tail.

b705.text: When living things grow, they increase in size. They also become more complex.

b706.text: You grow like that too. Bigger. And more complex: more hair, longer arms and legs, new teeth.

b707.text: Like animals, plants also increase in size and become more complex as they grow.

b708.text: A seed. A small plant. A bigger plant, with more leaves and flowers.

b802.text: One. A hen reproduces by laying eggs. Two. A tomato plant, by producing seeds. Three. A fern, by producing seeds.

b803.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

b805.text: Three. Those brown dots are spores.

b808.text: Fixed! A fern reproduces through spores.

b809.text: Showed three fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

b901.text: Three stamps! Grow: the chicks. Respond: the mimosa. Reproduce: the hen.

b903.text: Living things grow, respond to changes and reproduce.

c1003.text: Grow! Respond! Reproduce! That's what living things can DO!

b1001.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

b1002.text: Did you spot the lizard? It was on the hen house wall. Does a lizard lay eggs, or give birth to its young alive? Tell someone at home.

b1101.text: A hen. A cat. A tomato plant. A fern. There are millions of kinds of living things! But scientists sort them into only four groups. Can you guess the four? Lock in your answer for next time.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
